messages:
maria: hosted-usw2 pool-9 alert — p95 queueing climbed ~40% in last 12m, dashboard fired: https://dash.redwood/prod/pools/hosted-usw2-9 :warning:
ops-bot: [ALERT] pool=hosted-usw2-9 metric=p95_queue_ms value=1240ms duration=12m severity=warning. runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/pool-backpressure
chen: on it, looks like autoscaler decided not to add nodes at 03:10. pulling provisioning logs now
sam: paging infra oncall @maria @vikram — can you confirm if regional refill requests reached cloud?
maria: quick glance — provisioning API returned 504 at 2024-05-18T03:09:12Z then retries failed. snippet:
```
2024-05-18T03:09:12Z ERROR provisioning: launch request failed status=504 CloudAPI.Timeout request_id=abc-123
2024-05-18T03:09:18Z WARN provisioning: retrying launch (2/3)
```
vikram: confirmed. cloud account hit transient throttling while we were bumping quotas earlier today. support ticket #4231 is open (pending quota approval).
amelia: because nodes didn't come up, traffic spilled into our burst-slas pools which are much smaller. we applied an admission throttle (15%) at 03:14 to protect token latency SLOs — that's why you see reduced admission rate.
sam: what's the current backlog and trend?
maria: p95 token queue ~850ms, p99 ~2.1s. queued requests ~420. backlog increasing ~30 reqs/sec for the last 10m. also seeing ~12 evictions in past 20m which hurts KV cache warmup.
chen: digging deeper — autoscaler heuristics mis-evaluated usable slots because of slot fragmentation after the last rolling upgrade. scaler thought headroom was higher than reality. I pushed a patch to count partial slots and ignore recently-evicted nodes. rolling a canary to pool-9 now.
ops-bot: Deploy started: eng-infra/autoscaler v3.4.1 -> pool-9 (canary) by chen. CI: green. link: https://ci.redwood/build/9853
vikram: nice. cost question: if we lift the admission throttle to buy time, we'll serve more requests but risk p99s spiking and higher egress/compute costs. what are tradeoffs? :thinking_face:
amelia: prefer to keep throttle until canary proves stable. otherwise product will see many more timeouts/errors. we can notify product about degraded throughput.
sam: agreed. hold throttle for 10 more mins, monitor canary for changes to queue slope and eviction rate. set an alert if p99 > 3s or queued_count > 700.
chen: canary metrics: so far (03:18) admission up slightly, queued_count flattening in canary hosts. giving it 7–10m. if stable, I'll promote and trigger the quota request to be prioritized.
maria: next steps posted: 1) confirm canary success at 03:25; 2) if green, promote autoscaler and request emergency quota bump with cloud support; 3) keep admission at 85% until new nodes online. tagging #incident-notes.
vikram: also create a follow-up to adjust autoscaler test margins to include fragmentation scenarios. we shouldn't keep relying on manual throttles.
ops-bot: Note: ticket #4231 updated: "Requesting quota expedite due to live admission throttling impacting hosted-usw2 pool-9" by maria.
maria: thanks team. I'll prepare a short customer-facing note for support in case customers ask about degraded throughput.
sam: leaving oncall watch — ping here when promo done or if canary regress.
ops-bot: [STATUS] incident_state=investigating; impacted=hosted-usw2-9; mitigation=admission_throttle applied; next_check=03:25Z
amelia: adding postmortem template item: measure how often provisioning 504s correlate with autoscaler undershoot.
chen: canary looks stable at 03:24 — queued_count slope down, evictions reducing. promoting in 1m.
ops-bot: Deploy started: eng-infra/autoscaler v3.4.1 -> pool-9 (promote) by chen.
maria: promotion complete at 03:26. monitoring. admission throttle will be eased to 85% at 03:30 if metrics hold.
sam: marking this thread as ongoing. will update incident-notes when we confirm quotas are approved. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
